variants.name: 紧凑后掠
variants.specific: Hair direction: a compact windswept SHORT hair mass following the skull, made of TWO restrained angular locks swept slightly back. Hair scale less than half the old giant hair area. Clean forehead-to-hair transition, no high arch, no separate back banner, no long ponytail. The topmost guide star and its gold spine stay visible as a celestial crest above the compact head. Upper body: classical athletic archer with broad clear shoulder line, elegant collarbone and ONE chest plane, supple waist twist, 4-5 internal long planes maximum. Make arm silhouettes slender and powerful with readable elbow, not tapered plank ribbons. Aim for calm nobility and silhouette clarity.
variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a white geometric centaur archer on midnight navy. Input image 2 is ONLY a fixed gold constellation composition guide, registered by the square board. Create a materially more beautiful revision of the HUMAN UPPER BODY AND HAIR. Preserve the horse body, all FOUR horse legs, all four hooves, the short two-taper tail, lower-half geometry and the left-up arrow gesture from image 1. Keep the same square border, framing, scale and midnight navy background. The upper-body action can be proportionally reconstructed, including relocating the bow slightly, to fix the unnaturally long bow arm. Image 3 is an archery GEOMETRY GUIDE ONLY. On the 400x400 mm square board, the bow grip is at (145,89), draw hand and arrow nock at (215,121), bow top at about (166,25), bow bottom at about (173,196). The arrow shaft is one straight axis from the draw hand through the grip toward the upper-left guide chain near (79,62). Bowstrings connect both tips to the exact SAME draw-hand/nock point. Place the face and jaw naturally near the draw hand so the human is really drawing the bow, with anatomical upper-arm/forearm proportions. Do not preserve the old implausibly long arm. Never move any gold-guide nodes. Never output cyan guide marks or any text.
The old upper torso looks like stacked angular tubes and an awkward hanging triangle; the hair looks like a giant arched roof plus disconnected knife blades. Completely rethink shoulder, neck, chest, waist and hair while preserving the gesture: bow arm genuinely extends from shoulder to grip; draw hand, arrow nock, and the two bowstrings meet at ONE point; right elbow is drawn back. Give coherent noble athletic anatomy and a readable subtle torso twist that merges naturally into the horse. Use a few beautiful broad planes and long tapering contours, with deliberate quiet interiors. Hands one palm with thumb notch and one finger seam, blank elegant angular side profile with no eyes, ears, mouth detail or beard. All WHITE engraving strokes must be thin sharp straight line segments joined into graceful polygonal paths; no curves, no shading, no filled polygons, no little triangle mesh, no parallel ghost strokes. Keep the R1 angular style, don't turn it into a stick figure, generic logo, robot, armor or helmet.
Design WITH the fixed guide: right-side gold diagonals may act as shoulder/chest structural divisions, the upper gold spine above the head can remain an open celestial crest. Leave room for these gold lines; do not draw competing white diagonals just alongside every one. OUTPUT ONLY white centaur/bow/arrow artwork and thin grey square border on the original navy background. Do not output gold stars or gold lines; do not output guide markings, text or labels. The exact constellation will be applied from source coordinates afterwards. Make the upper body beautiful before minimizing engraving effort.
Hair direction: a compact windswept SHORT hair mass following the skull, made of TWO restrained angular locks swept slightly back. Hair scale less than half the old giant hair area. Clean forehead-to-hair transition, no high arch, no separate back banner, no long ponytail. The topmost guide star and its gold spine stay visible as a celestial crest above the compact head. Upper body: classical athletic archer with broad clear shoulder line, elegant collarbone and ONE chest plane, supple waist twist, 4-5 internal long planes maximum. Make arm silhouettes slender and powerful with readable elbow, not tapered plank ribbons. Aim for calm nobility and silhouette clarity.
Hair tips finish with short angled cuts and taper, not enormous spear points. Keep a 4-6 segment blank classical face profile; no eye or brow markings. Chest and waist facets should follow the fixed guide diagonal axes naturally, without making every star a joint. Use angular S-rhythm through shoulder, chest, waist and horse back, no accordion neck.

variants.name: 单束飘发
variants.specific: Hair direction: a clean low angular cap fitting the skull, connected to ONE elegant tapered swept-back hair bundle. The bundle rises gently backward toward the far-right upper guide star; use 2 or 3 long oblique facets, avoid a massive vertical curtain or forked blades. Total hair area about 40 percent of the old hair. No detached pieces. Upper body: more fluid and slender athlete, a clear diagonal shoulder axis and mild counter-twist at waist, three to five long chosen internal structural lines. Chest opens toward viewer while the head aims left. Neck connects naturally to shoulder instead of an accordion collar. Preserve impressive angularity while making the shoulder-arm-chest relationship graceful.

variants.name: 上扬发冠
variants.specific: Hair direction: an elegant compact upward-swept HAIR CREST, like one tapered flame made of TWO angular planes growing continuously from the crown. Reach upward along the upper guide star spine without a semicircular arch or roof; its lower hair mass stays fitted to the skull. One short backward taper only, no giant rear blade or helmet. The highest gold node remains an airy endpoint above the white crest. Upper body: refined abstract sculptural athlete with spacious chest, clear shoulder and neckline, only 3-4 broad facet seams, dignified balanced upper-body proportion and clean human-to-horse transition. Avoid low-poly triangle clutter; keep the bold R1 corners with a better rhythm.
